Linux, macOS and Android.

## Ground drawn from device-projected meshes (2026-11-08)

Patrick asked how hard dynamic shadows would be on `custom`, for buildings rather than sprites,
and then for a first step on a branch from `custom`. Shadow mapping needs the device to know where
each triangle lies in the world, and every vertex of the client reached it projected by the CPU
(`renderer_project_vertex`, `XYZRHW`). The houses' shadows on the ground are already in the map's
lightmaps; what is missing is shadow on the models themselves. This step moves the ground, the
largest and simplest static geometry, to meshes the device projects; models and the shadow pass
are not done.

- **The device API.** `render/gfx.h` gains `gfx_mesh_create`/`gfx_mesh_destroy` (world-space
  vertices with colour and two texture coordinates, 16-bit triangle-list indices),
  `gfx_set_world_view` and `gfx_draw_mesh`. `struct GfxWorldView` carries the CPU's own projection:
  the 4x3 view matrix, `proj[0..1]`, the screen centre, `RENDER_NEAR_Z` and
  `RENDER_DEPTH_SCALE`, so a point lands on the pixel and depth `project_vertex` gives it, and the
  fog start and end that reproduce `rp_vertex_fog_alpha` (`renderer_world_view` in
  `rp_project.c`, which also covers its case of fog near equal to far). Direct3D 9 draws a mesh
  through the fixed-function pipeline: the view matrix as `D3DTS_VIEW`, a projection built from
  the current viewport, linear vertex fog on the view depth (range fog off) and lighting off, set
  around the draw and put back after it. The vertex and index buffers are `D3DPOOL_MANAGED`; the
  mesh keeps its arrays, and the three places that release the device drop its buffers so the
  next draw makes them on the new device. The GL vertex shader has a mesh branch: one matrix to
  the pre-transformed vertex's pixel space times the view depth, then the same pixel-centre
  mapping as before, and the fog factor from the depth, rounded down to a step as the CPU's is.
  The buffers are made on the first draw, on the main thread, as textures are.
- **The original's vertex-buffer path goes.** `gfx_draw_vbuffer`, `gfx_vbuffer`, `struct RPMesh`,
  `struct VertexBuffer`, the `RENDER_OPAQUE_MESH`/`RENDER_ALPHA_MESH`/`RENDER_OVERLAY_MESH` queues,
  their flushes and the `l_opaque_mesh`/`l_alpha_mesh` timing phases had no producer; the one
  mesh queue now is `RENDER_GROUND_MESH`.
- **The ground.** `world/ground_draw.c` builds a mesh per block of 32 by 32 cells on the ground's
  first draw (`GND_GPU_BLOCK`, at most 12,288 vertices): four vertices and two triangles per
  surface in the corner order of `c3d_ground15_draw_surface`'s strip, grouped into runs of one
  texture and one lightmap page. `c3d_ground15_render` queues each block that shares a cell with
  the scene-graph leaf once a frame, with `renderer_add_mesh_draw`, and `flush_ground_mesh`
  draws them right after the ground's two-texture quads, with their states. The device clips what
  the CPU path left out with `off_screen` and `behind_eye`. Water keeps its per-cell loop.
- **When the CPU path stays.** The meshes hold each surface's own colour, which the CPU path uses
  only while lightmaps are on, the two-texture path is supported and the weather colour is
  exactly white (`g_weather.color` is 1, so the scaling changes nothing); otherwise the whole
  ground takes the old path that frame. Surfaces with `halfAlpha` take colour alpha 0x80 there
  unless the player is blind, so they stay on the CPU path then and join the meshes while the
  player is blind.
- **Depth ties.** The device rounds the depth differently from `project_vertex`, by a few steps
  of the depth buffer, and the ground is drawn after the models with `LESSEQUAL`. Where a model
  lies on the ground (Prontera's flower beds, which z-fight with it in the original too) a row of
  pixels changes sides. A bias of 2^-20 to push the ground back was tried: it kept the flower
  beds' edges but flipped many more of the z-fighting pixels (954 instead of 82 in
  `prontera_crowd`), so the meshes use none.

Validation, in `C:\Users\Patrick Kuhlmann\GIT\client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: all twelve scene
captures from a scene build of the unchanged objects repeat exactly, and the meshes' captures
differ from them by at most one colour step (the fog factor, which the fixed-function pipeline
does not round down) except in the flower beds' z-fighting: 82 pixels in `prontera_crowd` and 182
or 183 in each of the six captures of `granny_dead`, `granny_models`, `guild_flags` and
`hunter_traps` (all in Prontera), none in `camera_level_view`, `iz_int03_enter`, `keyboard` and
`windows_open`. `build.bat check` passes (1,822 files in 22 libraries, 1,151 objects), and so does
the full `tests\build.bat`. `test_projection` now checks that `renderer_world_view` puts points on
the pixels and depths of `renderer_project_vertex`, with the fog of `rp_vertex_fog_alpha` to one
step, for three fog ranges, near equal to far among them; `test_renderer_storage` feeds the
ground-mesh queue and counts the queues with `RENDER_PASS_COUNT`, its render digests as before, and
`test_effect_trace` keeps the digest `2842b5a04b52ece4`. `gfx_gl.c` compiles without warnings
against SDL3's headers (x64 `cl /W3`); it was not run, and `test_gfx_gl` draws no mesh. Not run
either: `x64`, `freetype` and `libs` builds, CMake, Linux, macOS and Android. Next: the models
(`model_node_render.c`, whose colours follow blindness, highlight, the actor's alpha and the
ground lighting per frame), then a shadow-map pass from the map's light direction.

## Model faces drawn from device-projected meshes, and the weather colour (2026-11-08)

Patrick asked for the models next. A model node's faces are lit once when the model is placed
(`c3d_node_light`: `FaceInfo` colours and the ground-lit `lightInts`), so like the ground they
can live in a static mesh; what changes per frame is the node's matrix and a few states.

- **What goes into a node's mesh.** `world/model_node_render.c` builds it on the node's first
  draw: three vertices per face with the position, the `FaceInfo` texture coordinates and the
  colour `face_colours` gives (the `lightInts` while `g_weather.ground_lighting` is on, the
  `FaceInfo` colour otherwise, alpha 0xff), grouped into runs of one texture, one-sided and
  twoSided apart. Faces of an alpha-keyed texture (format 1) stay out, as do version 2 faces whose
  texture has a texture-coordinate animation (`uv_xform_find`): those go into the sorted alpha
  lists or need new coordinates every frame. A node with more than 21,845 faces or a corner
  outside its vertices keeps the CPU path. The mesh is rebuilt when `ground_lighting` changes.
- **When it is drawn.** While the actor is opaque (alpha 0xff), the player is not blind (that
  path uses the weather tint) and the node is not highlighted; otherwise the node's faces take the
  old path that frame. The mesh's draws go into `RENDER_MODEL_MESH`, flushed right after
  `RENDER_OPAQUE_CLAMP` with its states, where those faces' quads went. The faces the mesh holds are
  skipped in the CPU loops, and a node whose faces are all in it skips the CPU projection.
- **Projection and culling.** A child node is drawn with its parent's matrix to view space as its
  "view", so each node's own matrix to view space (`m`, the one `project()` uses) is the mesh's
  view matrix; no separate model matrix is needed. The CPU loops cull by the screen winding, and the
  two versions test it opposite ways: version 1 keeps the faces that turn counter-clockwise on
  screen (y down), version 2 the clockwise ones, swapped for a mirrored actor (`mirrored`, from the
  signs of its scale), and twoSided faces are kept either way. The draws carry the matching cull
  mode (`GFX_CULL_CW`, the new `GFX_CULL_CCW`, or none), which `flush_mesh_queue` sets and puts
  back.
- **The weather colour on the device.** The ground and the models drew from meshes only while
  `g_weather.color` was white, but that colour is `1 - (1 - ambient) * (1 - diffuse)` of the map's
  own light, white only where one of them is, and it changes while weather darkens the light; the
  indoor map `iz_int03` never used the meshes. `struct GfxWorldView` gains `colourScale`, which
  `renderer_add_mesh_draw` takes with each draw. GL multiplies and rounds down in the vertex shader
  as `face_colours` and `c3d_ground15_draw_surface` do. Direct3D 9 turns on fixed-function
  lighting for a draw whose scale is not white, with the global ambient light set to the scale, the
  material's ambient colour and alpha from the vertex, no emissive or specular and light 0 off, so
  the colour is the vertex colour times the scale to within a step; the states, the material and
  light 0 are put back after the draw. A white scale draws without lighting, as before.
- **Destroying a mesh** no longer flushes the vertex batch; meshes are made, drawn and destroyed on
  the drawing thread, as `gfx.h` now says.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the same captures of the unchanged
objects (pixels differing by more than one step, then by more than 16):

| capture | > 1 | > 16 |
|---|---|---|
| `prontera_crowd` | 1,176 | 114 |
| `granny_dead` (2), `granny_models`, `guild_flags` (2), `hunter_traps` | 242 to 272 | 209 to 231 |
| `camera_level_view`, moving and still | 17 and 244 | 12 and 204 |
| `iz_int03_enter`, `keyboard`, `windows_open` | 12, 3, 10 | 6, 2, 4 |

In `prontera_crowd`, 1,095 of them are new against the ground-only build, nearly all off by two to
seven steps in the water over the fountain's basin (the basin's texture coordinates interpolated a
little differently under the blend). The others are the flower beds' row, rows of single pixels
along thin model edges, and places where a ground cell's wall and a model's face lie in one plane;
no face is missing or added. `iz_int03` is now drawn from the meshes, and about 40,000 of its
pixels differ by one step (the scale's rounding), the rest on the edges of a hanging chain.
`build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass; `test_renderer_storage` queues a model
draw with a cull mode as well, and `test_projection` checks the colour scale `renderer_world_view`
passes on. Not run: GL, `x64`, `freetype`, `libs`, CMake and the other platforms. No frame-time
measurement was made.

## Shadows on the models (2026-11-08)

Patrick asked for the shadow pass after the models moved to device-projected meshes. The ground's
lightmaps already hold the shadows the map's editor baked for the buildings, so only the models
receive the new shadows; on the ground they would darken what is already dark. Only the models'
opaque meshes cast them.

- **The colour in shadow.** A model face's lit colour is the map's ambient plus its diffuse light
  times the face's N.L, baked when the model is placed (`c3d_node_light`). It now also stores,
  per face corner, the colour without the diffuse part: `C3dNode.shadowColours` beside the
  `FaceInfo` colours (the ambient times the same 128-or-255 factor; unlit models, shade type 0,
  keep their own colour) and `shadowGround` beside `lightInts` (the ground's cell colour added as
  for the lit one). The mesh vertex carries it as `GfxMeshVertex.shadow`, which Direct3D 9 reads
  as the specular colour. A face turned away from the light has the same two colours, so it does
  not darken twice.
- **The shadow map.** `renderer_shadow_frame` (`rp_project.c`), called from `view_on_render`,
  builds an orthographic view along the map's light over a square of 1.5 times the camera's
  distance (200 to 2,500 units) around the point it looks at, 3,000 units deep either way, as a
  matrix from view space (the space every model draw already reaches with its own matrix) to the
  light's. The renderer keeps the light from `renderer_set_light`. `flush_opaque_lists` first draws
  this frame's `RENDER_MODEL_MESH` draws into the shadow map (`gfx_shadow_begin`/`gfx_shadow_end`),
  then draws them with `gfx_shadow_receive` on.
- **Which way the light points.** The map's light vector is the direction the light travels:
  Prontera's is (0.5, 0.707, 0.5), and +y is down in the world. Taken as the direction towards the
  light, the shadow map looked up from under the map and darkened every face that looks up (the
  fountain's basin floor came out black in a view of the shadow test alone).
- **Direct3D 9.** The fixed-function pipeline cannot compare depths, so the shadow pass and the
  receiving draws use the backend's first shaders, HLSL compiled at the first shadow frame by
  `D3DCompile` from `d3dcompiler_47.dll` (Windows 8.1 and later carry it; loaded with
  `LoadLibrary`, so the build needs nothing new) for `vs_2_0`/`ps_2_0`. The shadow pass writes the
  light depth into a 2048 by 2048 `R32F` render target with its own D24X8 depth surface; the
  receiving pixel shader does what the stages do for an opaque mesh (texture times colour, the
  colour scaled by the weather colour and rounded down as before) and blends between the shadow and
  the lit colour by four shadow-map taps interpolated by the sample's place between texels. The
  alpha test stays fixed-function, and so does the fog, from the vertex shader's fog output. Both
  targets are `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT`, dropped before a reset and wherever the device is released, and
  made again on the next shadow frame; the shaders go with the device. Without the DLL, without an
  `R32F` render target, or with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`, `gfx_shadow_begin` answers 0 and the models are
  drawn as before. The GL backend answers 0 for now.
- **Bias and filtering.** A pixel counts as lit while it lies no more than 4 world units behind
  the depth in the map. With 2 units, faces at a slant to the light shadowed themselves in places;
  8 looked the same as 4 on the lit faces. Four taps at half a texel (point samples averaged) left
  the statue's shadow in the fountain in steps of a texel (about 0.8 units at the default zoom);
  weighting the four nearest texels by the sample's position smooths it.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: the house's roof overhang now shades the
wall under it, the statue throws a soft shadow into the basin, and the towers' sides away from the
light keep their colour. Against the unchanged objects, 47,846 pixels of `prontera_crowd` differ by
more than a step, 43,939 to 45,631 in the other Prontera scenes, 8,170 and 11,550 in
`camera_level_view`, and 2,962, 2,972 and 312 on `iz_int03` (`iz_int03_enter`, `keyboard`,
`windows_open`; a second run moved the first two by about ten pixels). A view of the shadow test alone (lit
white, shadowed black) was checked on `prontera_crowd` and `camera_level_view`. `build.bat check`
and the full `tests\build.bat` pass; `test_renderer_storage` stubs the shadow calls. Not done:
shadows from models outside the view (only the frame's model draws cast, so a shadow can end at
the screen's edge), shadows on the ground, sprites or effects, the GL backend, a frame-time
measurement, and a setting in the options window.

## Sharper shadows: cascades, steady texels, offset and soft edges (2026-11-09)

Patrick found the first shadows blocky and asked for shadows that look exact on Direct3D 9: a
map fitted to the view, more texels, cascades, texels that stay put, and a bias that holds on
slanted surfaces. Seeing them sharp, he asked for the soft border the first, coarse map had.

- **Why they were blocky.** One 2048 map covered a square of 1.5 times the camera's distance in
  radius, about 1,700 units across in `prontera_crowd`: 0.8 units a texel, while one world unit is
  about six screen pixels at the default zoom (RO's view is 15 degrees high), so a texel covered
  about five pixels. Most of the square lay off screen.
- **Fitted cascades.** `renderer_shadow_frame` now cuts the view into four slices of view depth
  (`GFX_SHADOW_CASCADES`), between where the view's four corner rays enter and leave a band from
  300 units above to 60 below the camera's focus (+y down), where the receiving models stand, no
  further than four times the camera's distance (at most 8,000). The slices grow with the depth
  (0.7 of the way from even to geometric steps). Each cascade's map covers its slice's part of the
  band as the light sees it, plus a margin, in its own 2048 by 2048 `R32F` target; the four share
  one depth surface (80 MB with it, where one 4096 map with its depth surface takes 128 MB and
  spends the same texels evenly). The light's map is orthographic, so a caster off screen that
  shades something in view lands on the same place of the map and is kept; only its depth range
  (3,000 units either way) bounds it. By the view's geometry (not measured), a texel at the default
  view is now about 0.15 units, under a screen pixel.
- **Choosing a cascade per pixel** needs dynamic branching, so the receiving shaders move to
  `vs_3_0`/`ps_3_0`; the backend asks for shader model 3 (in hardware vertex processing) and
  `GFX_SHADOW_SIZE` textures and draws no shadows without them. Shader model 3 leaves the fog to
  the pixel shader, which blends towards `D3DRS_FOGCOLOR` while `D3DRS_FOGENABLE` is on, by the
  same linear factor. The shadow pass still uses `vs_2_0`/`ps_2_0`, once per cascade
  (`gfx_shadow_cascade`).
- **Steady texels.** A cascade's half size is rounded up to a multiple of 8 units and its centre
  kept to whole texels, so its texels stay put while the camera moves and edges do not crawl.
- **Offset and bias.** Each model vertex now carries its face's normal
  (`GfxMeshVertex.nx`/`ny`/`nz`, `D3DFVF_NORMAL`; zero for the ground, which does not receive). The
  receiving vertex shader moves the lookup off the surface towards the light by 1.5 texels times
  the sine of the angle between the surface and the light, and the constant bias stays 4 units: at
  1 unit, Prontera's flower beds, which lay their flowers a unit or two over the grass, shaded the
  grass under them.
- **Soft edges.** The lookup is the share of 16 points on a disc of 0.5 units radius that are lit
  (point samples of the map), so edges fade over about a unit, as the first coarse map blurred
  them. Over that disc a slanted surface moves along the light, which shaded a band of a beam that
  lies at a steep angle to it, so the bias grows by the disc's radius times the tangent of the
  slant (up to 8 times). With a radius of 1.5 the edges spread over three units and the shadows of
  thin casters, such as a lamp post's across the fountain, faded away.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, captures compared with the first shadow
build and with each step: the statue's and the lamp post's shadows in the fountain keep their
shapes with smooth edges instead of steps of a texel; the house's beam keeps its shadow (its
brightness across the edge measured the same in all three builds); the flower bed shows no shadow
of its own flowers. Against the unchanged objects, 39,575 pixels of `prontera_crowd` differ by
more than a step, 30,237 to 32,027 in the other Prontera scenes, 46,272 and 85,752 in
`camera_level_view`, and 2,585, 2,559 and 306 on `iz_int03`. A view of the shadow test alone (lit
white, shadowed black) found the band the soft edges shaded on the beam and showed it gone with the
slope bias. `build.bat check` and the full
`tests\build.bat` pass. Not done: shadows from models outside the frame's draws, the GL backend,
a frame-time measurement, and a setting for the softness.

## The shadow maps replace the baked shadows (2026-11-09)

Patrick asked for the moving windmill sails at yuno_fild01's south gate to shade the ground, and
then said what the shadow maps are for: to replace the shadows the map's editor baked into the
lightmaps, matching them.

- **One map for models and ground.** The ground's meshes now cast into the shadow maps as the
  models' do (each ground surface gets its face's normal, so the offset and the slope bias work on
  it), and both receive them. A first version kept a second set of maps, cast only by animated
  model nodes, for the ground alone, so that it would not darken the baked shadows twice; with
  the baked shadows replaced there is nothing to darken twice, and it went.
- **The ground's receiving shader** (`ground_hlsl`, `GFX_SHADOW_GROUND`) does what its two stages
  do, lightmap colour plus intensity times texture times colour, but takes the intensity as lit
  down to the darkness of a shadow and lets the shadow maps darken it instead; texels darker than
  a shadow keep their own darkness (`saturate(intensity / darkness)`). Where the shadow maps are
  not drawn (no shader model 3, `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`, the GL backend, a surface on the CPU path),
  the baked shadows stay as before.
- **How dark.** The baked intensities are two levels: 128 in shadow, 255 in the sun, some 45
  percent of the texels each in the GNDs of yuno_fild01, prontera and iz_int03, the rest on the
  edges between. A shadow is therefore half the lit colour (`SHADOW_DARKNESS`, 128/255), for the
  ground and the models alike. That replaces the colour without the diffuse light that each model
  corner (`shadowColours`, `shadowGround`) and ground corner carried before, which was darker than
  the baked shadows (the map's ambient alone, 0.3 at yuno_fild01); the vertex loses that colour.
- **Which way.** The light vector is the direction the light travels. Mirroring x was tried after
  one windmill's shadow seemed to fall the wrong way, but it had been compared with another
  windmill's baked shadow: a test build drew, on every ground pixel, the baked intensity and the
  shadow test side by side, and the share of pixels shaded in both over those shaded in either
  came to 0.49, 0.72 and 0.37 on `yuno_gate`, `prontera_crowd` and `camera_level_view` as it is,
  against 0.29, 0.09 and 0.25 with x mirrored, and at most 0.35 with z or both.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: side by side with the unchanged objects, the
shadows on the ground of the three maps fall where the baked ones did, about as dark; the
windmill's sails shade the grass as they turn. `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat`
pass. Not done: alpha-keyed faces (tree leaves) and texture-animated faces do not cast, models
outside the frame's draws and models fading, highlighted or seen blind do not cast, the ground's
half-alpha surfaces keep the baked shadows and its water takes none, and the models' ground-lit colours
(`lightInts`, from the lightmap under them) still carry the baked shadows.

## Shadows through alpha, and from models drawn on the CPU (2026-11-09)

With the baked shadows replaced, whatever does not cast loses its shadow. Two gaps followed from
the meshes' shape:

- **Alpha.** The models' opaque lists draw with the alpha test at 0xcf, so a texture with an
  alpha channel, such as the cloth and lattice of yuno_fild01's windmill sails or tree leaves, shows
  only its opaque texels; the shadow pass drew the whole faces and the sails cast solid
  rectangles. A draw with a texture bound to stage 0 now goes through a second depth shader pair
  (`depthAlphaPass`/`depthAlphaColour`, `vs_2_0`/`ps_2_0`) that drops the texels under 207/255,
  and the models' mesh draws are cast with their textures: the sails' shadows on the grass now
  have the baked ones' shape.
- **Faces outside the mesh, and frames without it.** Each node also gets `casterMesh`, which only
  casts: its alpha-keyed faces (format 1, which the alpha lists draw) with their texture, and its
  faces with a texture-coordinate animation without one. Its draws, and the node's mesh in a
  frame whose colour takes the CPU path (the actor fading, the node highlighted, the player
  blind), go into `RENDER_SHADOW_ONLY`, which only the shadow pass draws, so a building does not
  lose its shadow while it fades. The two meshes share their making (`gpu_mesh_from`).

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: on `yuno_gate` the alpha test changed 75,674
pixels against the build before it, where the sails' and trees' shadows on the grass now follow
their textures as the baked ones did. `casterMesh` and the shadow-only frames of fading or
highlighted nodes changed no pixel of these scenes (none of them has an alpha-keyed caster in
view or a fading building), so they are built and queued but not seen in a capture.
`build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass; `test_renderer_storage` feeds the new
queue.

## Every model face from the mesh, and shaders for every mesh (2026-11-09)

Patrick asked what still had to be kept in step with the CPU path, then to work through the list.
The first item was the nodes split between the two paths: a node drew some textures from its mesh
and the rest on the CPU (`inMesh`, `allInMesh`), fell back to the CPU entirely while it faded, was
highlighted or the player was blind, and cast from a second mesh (`casterMesh`) through a
shadow-only queue. All of that came from four things the CPU did per vertex (the actor's alpha,
the highlight, the blind tint, texture-coordinate animation) and from the alpha-texture faces,
which have to sort with the other alpha quads.

- **Shaders only.** Fixed-function Direct3D 9 could give the draw a colour scale only through its
  lighting, and could not reproduce the clamped lighting the next step needs, so a mesh is now
  drawn by shaders alone: `gfx_mesh_create` compiles them for the device's first mesh
  (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, shader model 3) and answers NULL without them, and the ground and the
  models then take the CPU path. The model and ground draws share one vertex shader
  (`meshVertex`); the shadow maps sit on samplers 2 to 5 for both, and are sampled only while
  `gfx_shadow_receive(1)` is on, which the renderer turns on after drawing the maps and off at the
  end of the frame; otherwise the cascades' far depths are 0 and every pixel counts as lit. The
  fixed-function mesh path, its material and light-0 handling are gone. The scale rounds down
  exactly in the shader, where fixed-function lighting came within a step.
- **A draw's own state.** `struct GfxMeshDraw` carries what the stages would do (`kind`: model or
  ground), the vertex colour to use (`second`: a vertex now has `diffuse` and `colour2`), a colour
  whose red, green and blue scale the vertex colour, rounded down as before, and whose alpha
  multiplies its alpha, and a 2x3 transform of the first texture's coordinates.
  `GfxWorldView.colourScale` moved into it.
- **One mesh per node, every face.** The mesh holds all of a node's faces, sorted into draws of one
  texture and one `twoSided`; `diffuse` is the ground-lit colour (`lightInts`) and `colour2` the
  node's own (`FaceInfo`), both opaque. Each frame `gpu_render` gives every draw what
  `face_colours` and the loops give its faces' quads: the weather colour, or the weather tint and
  the node's own colour for a blind player, the node's own colour also while ground lighting is
  off (so the mesh no longer has to be rebuilt when it changes), the actor's alpha, and on a
  version 2 node its texture-coordinate animation as the transform `uv_turn_matrix` makes from
  `uv_turn`'s steps. Its list flags are the loops' own, and `renderer_mesh_pass` maps them to the
  queue `renderer_add_prim` would use (`RENDER_OPAQUE_CLAMP`, `_WRAP`, `RENDER_ALPHA_CLAMP`,
  `_WRAP`, `_WRITE_DEPTH`); in an alpha list the draw is keyed by the rhw of its first face's
  first corner, as a quad by its first vertex. The CPU loops stay for a node whose mesh cannot be
  made.
- **Mesh draws among the quads.** A `RenderEntry` now says whether it holds a mesh draw;
  `flush_plain` and `flush_keyed` draw those with `draw_mesh_entry` (world view when it changes,
  cull mode set and put back, textures), so they are sorted and drawn with the quads of their list
  and its states, two-pass alpha included. `RENDER_MODEL_MESH` is gone and `RENDER_SHADOW_ONLY`
  became `RENDER_SHADOW_CASTERS`, which every model draw also goes into; the ground's draws stay in
  `RENDER_GROUND_MESH` and cast from there. Casters are drawn without their cull modes.
- **The highlight.** `C3dNode.highlight` was only read and cleared; nothing in this tree sets it,
  on `main` either. It and its colours in `face_colours` are removed.

No model in this tree fades: `world_model_create` sets every model actor's `pickable` to 0, so
`c3d_actor_pick` and `fade` never change its alpha, and the alpha path was checked through the
alpha-texture draws instead.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1` (pixels differing by more than one step, then
by more than 16). Against the CPU-only build, with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`: `prontera_crowd` 1,176
and 114, `camera_level_view` 244 and 204 (moving 942 and 641), `granny_models` 242 and 206,
`guild_flags` 244 to 247 and 208, `yuno_gate` 21 to 23 and 15 to 17, as with the old path, and
`iz_int03_enter` 3 and 2 (12 and 6 before, the exact rounding). Against the build before, with
shadows: 0 in `prontera_crowd`, `camera_level_view` and the six `yuno_gate` frames, 3 to 22 in
`granny_models`, `guild_flags` and `iz_int03_enter`, and 615 in `camera_level_view_moving`, a row
along a flower bed's top edge where two faces at one depth meet and the other one now wins, since
the model draws sort with the opaque quads by texture. Six spots on maps built from version 2
models, where a temporary log showed alpha-texture draws in four (`wolfvill` twice, `ba_maison`,
`nif_dun01`) and animated texture coordinates in two of them, differ from the CPU-only build in 0
to 298 pixels, seams where two faces meet at one depth; the animated and alpha faces themselves
match. `test_model_mesh_load` checks `uv_turn_matrix` against `uv_turn`; `test_renderer_storage`
queues a model draw into an alpha list. Not seen in a capture: a blind player. Not run: GL,
`x64`, `freetype`, CMake and the other platforms.

## Shadows that know the model's light, and the map's own shadow strength (2026-11-09)

The second item: the models' faces carry the light of the map (`c3d_node_light`: diffuse times
the cosine to the light plus ambient, clamped to 1, times 128 or 255 by the texture vertex) and
the ground's colour under them, and the shadow maps then multiplied the whole colour by 128/255
wherever a face lay in shadow. Since the shadow pass casts from both sides of every face, a face
turned away from the light always lies in shadow, and it was darkened twice: Prontera's tower
showed its shaded side at 107 instead of 118 (mean grey of the patch).

- **The map's shadow strength.** The RSW light block's last float, which the client skipped, is
  the share of the light the map's editor took away in the shadows it baked: across the maps of
  `client-files` the lightmaps' shadow intensity is about 255 times one minus it (izlude 0.6 bakes
  104, lighthalzen 0.4 bakes 156, nif_fild01 0.7 bakes 80, job_prist 0.2 bakes 208, ra_fild03
  0.55 bakes 116; 754 maps hold 0.5, and prontera, yuno_fild01 and iz_int03 bake 128, the
  constant used so far). A few maps hold a
  value their lightmaps were not baked with (ve_fild06 holds 0.4 and bakes 128). `c3d_world_res_load`
  now reads it as `shadowOpacity` (0.5 for maps before version 1.7), `renderer_set_light` takes
  it, and the shadow's darkness is one minus it; at darkness 1 (61 maps hold 0) no shadow map is
  drawn, as their editor baked none.
- **A model face in shadow.** The vertex shader works out two colours per corner: the lit one, the
  CPU's exactly, and the shadowed one, the corner's own lit colour times the darkness but no less
  than ambient times its share of the light (128 or 255; 0 for a model lit without the light),
  what `c3d_node_light` gives a face turned away from the light, before the ground's light is
  added; the pixel shader mixes them by how much of the pixel is lit. A face turned away from the
  light keeps its colour in shadow, a face towards it darkens as the ground does, and no face
  ends darker than its ambient light. Without receiving, the mix is the lit colour alone.
- **The vertex colours.** `diffuse` now holds the node's own colour with the share of the light as
  its alpha, `colour2` the ground's light under the corner; `GfxMeshDraw.second` became
  `lightGround`, which adds it (at most 255 a channel). `C3dNode.lightInts`, the sum of both, became
  `groundLight`, the ground's light alone, and `face_colours` adds it (`ground_lit`), so the CPU
  path draws as before.
- **Receiving off** now sets the ground's darkness to 1, so the baked shadows stay as they are; a
  frame without a shadow pass after one with it took the darkness of the last.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0` every capture
(`prontera_crowd`, `camera_level_view` both, `granny_models`, `guild_flags` both,
`iz_int03_enter`, six `yuno_gate` frames) is the same as before, pixel for pixel. With shadows,
the patch on Prontera's tower reads 117 (118 without shadows, 107 before); on `yuno_gate` the
towers' shaded sides look as without shadows again; on
`izlude` (opacity 0.6) the shadowed ground is 0.78 to 0.80 times as bright as before (0.4 over
0.502).
`build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass; `test_model_lighting` checks the ground's
light and the sums `face_colours` makes from it. Not run: GL, `x64`, `freetype`, CMake.

## Shadows from what the camera does not see (2026-11-09)

The third item: the shadow pass drew the casters the camera's pass had queued, so a building or a
lamp post just out of view cast nothing into it, and shadows popped in at the screen's edges and
from behind the camera. (The entry before this one took the darker ground at the lower right of
its `izlude` capture for a shadow baked from a building out of view; it is a darker stone
texture, the same with and without shadows, and that sentence is removed.)

- **Where a caster can be.** The light map is orthographic, so a caster shades a cascade wherever
  it lies along the light, as long as it lies across the light inside the cascade's square.
  `renderer_shadow_frame` keeps the light's axes, each cascade's square and the depth kept along
  the light (`struct ShadowReach`); `renderer_shadow_reaches` tests a box, given by its centre,
  half sizes and axes, against them.
- **A second walk of the world.** After the camera's pass, `view_on_render` walks the scene graph
  with that test (`view_cast_shadows`): from a leaf it reaches, each model whose oriented box it
  reaches and that has not queued its casters this frame (`C3dActor.castFrame`, set by `render`
  and the new `cast`) queues only its casters (`ModelActorOps.cast`, `c3d_node_v1_cast`,
  `c3d_node_v2_cast`), and the leaf's ground queues its blocks' (`c3d_ground15_cast`). Such a model
  is ticked once that frame, as the camera's pass ticks the ones in the leaves it visits, so its
  animation, and its shadow's, keep going while only its shadow is in view; the original ticks
  only the models of the camera's leaves.
- **One caster per ground block.** A block's plain surfaces now cast as one untextured draw
  (`castCount` indices, once a frame: `castFrame`) into `RENDER_SHADOW_CASTERS`, which the models'
  casters share; `RENDER_GROUND_MESH` no longer casts, and the shadow pass draws that one queue.
  The surfaces with half alpha, which only a blind player sees, still cast nothing.
- A formatting slip from the first item is fixed: two statements of `gpu_render` shared a line.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the build before, with shadows:
`camera_level_view` 5,463 pixels (moving 7,478), a shadow from behind the camera now on the
street at the bottom; `izlude` 2,343, a post's shadow at the left edge whose post stands just out
of view; `prontera_crowd` 497; `granny_models` and `guild_flags` 3; `iz_int03_enter` and the six
`yuno_gate` frames 0. `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass. Not measured: the
frame time of the second walk and the extra casters.

## Water projected by the device (2026-11-09)

The fourth item was water and the ground's surfaces with half alpha.

- **Half alpha.** Only `c3d_ground15_check_alpha` sets `GndSurface.halfAlpha`, and its one caller
  (`game/input.c`) runs it only while `ray_tests_cells` is on, which `game/map_entry.c` sets to 0
  and nothing sets otherwise, so no surface has half alpha in this tree. The meshes' handling of
  them (`plainCount`, `half`) stays, so they would still be drawn the CPU's way if one had.
- **Why water is not a mesh.** Each water cell is its own quad in the alpha lists, sorted by the
  rhw of its first corner among the sprites and effects there, which do not write depth: where a
  character wades, the cells nearer than its feet are drawn over them. A mesh drawn a block at a
  time would sort as one, and the heights change every frame (`ground_water_height` by the
  cell's diagonal, from a table of whole degrees). So the CPU keeps building the quads.
- **World-space quads.** A new vertex kind, `GFX_VTX_WORLD`, has `GFX_VTX_TEX1`'s layout with x, y
  and z in world coordinates, which the device takes through the camera's world view
  (`gfx_set_world_camera`, set at the start of `renderer_draw_lists` from the view
  `renderer_set_camera` stored in `view_on_render`) to the pixel and depth the CPU would have
  given them. Direct3D 9 draws them with a `vs_2_0` vertex shader (`worldVertex`) and the
  fixed-function pixel stages, so every stage, blend and alpha state of the lists applies as
  before, the fog coming from the specular alpha as for a pre-transformed vertex; the batch keeps
  them apart from the pre-transformed ones. GL draws them with the mesh branch of its vertex
  shader. `RPQuad.world` marks such a quad (reset by every pool take); `draw_quad` passes the kind.
- **Water's quads.** `water_quad` still projects the four corners to make its decisions (a corner
  behind the eye, a quad facing away, the alpha list's key and the vertex fog, both from the rhw),
  then hands the device the corners' world coordinates while the ground is drawn from meshes; the
  CPU-only path is unchanged.
- **A fix to the third item.** `renderer_shadow_frame` set up the frame's shadows, and with them
  the second walk of the world, even where the device draws none (`RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`, no shader
  model 3, GL): the walk then ticked models out of view for no shadow, and a swinging bell in
  `camera_level_view_moving` stood at another angle than without the walk. It now asks
  `gfx_shadows_supported` first, which `shadow_prepare` uses as well.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: against the build before, with shadows,
every capture is the same pixel for pixel, `prontera_crowd` with the water in the fountain's basin
among them; with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0` every capture is the same as the second item's, and so
against the CPU-only build as in the entries before. The two `alberta` spots captured show no water. `build.bat check` and the full
`tests\build.bat` pass. Not run: GL.

## Granny models projected by the device; sprites and effects stay (2026-11-09)

The fifth item was sprites and effects. A survey of what the CPU still projects showed three
kinds of thing:

- **Granny models** (`actor/granny.c`: the 3D actors, guild guardians among them) are skinned on
  the CPU each frame and their triangles projected corner by corner, like the water's: true
  world-space geometry. Their three drawing loops now also hand the device each corner's world
  coordinates (`world_corner`, through the matrix the view follows in the corner's projection)
  and mark the quad (`granny_projection_submit`'s new `world`), keeping the projected rhw for
  the list's fog. They do so only while `renderer_world_quads` answers 1: the view they are drawn
  with is the frame's camera view (`renderer_set_camera`), so a granny model drawn with another
  view keeps the CPU's way, and the device can draw world-space quads.
- **Effects** (`effects/rag`, about 170 call sites of `prim_project_vertex` and `prim_draw_quad`)
  project their corners and then work on them in screen space: `quad_depth` biases a quad's depth
  through its rhw (`PRIM_QUAD_DEPTH_BIAS`), puts it in front of everything with z 1e-9
  (`PRIM_QUAD_IN_FRONT`) or rebuilds it upright around its projected centre, widened in pixels
  (`PRIM_QUAD_UPRIGHT`); particles and the flying shapes add offsets in pixels.
- **Sprites** project one anchor and build the billboard in pixels around it, with the depth of
  each row set from the screen row (the billboard entries of `README.md`).

Neither keeps a second copy of its geometry's projection to remove: what the device would do
for them is screen-space work each kind defines for itself, and moving it to the device means
writing each kind's vertex arithmetic again as shader code, with no pixel parity to check it
against. They stay on the CPU. The CPU's projection itself stays in any case, for anchors, names,
gauges and picking.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the build before, with and without
shadows: `granny_models` 7 pixels (edges of the guardians), `guild_flags` 2, everything else the
same (`prontera_crowd` differs only where the mouse pointer was caught in one capture).
`build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass; `renderer_granny_projection_test.h` checks
that a quad submitted without `world` is not marked.

## The ground under models it touches keeps its baked shadow (2026-11-09)

Patrick saw Prontera's flower beds, from further away, striped with pale bands. The bed
(`나무잡초꽃\둥근꽃밭.rsm`, scale 1 at the plaza's own height) lays a grass plane 0.3 units and its
flowers 0.2 to 2.4 units over the plaza's cobblestones, which show between them; the editor baked
those cobblestones in shadow, so the gaps read as grey soil. The shadow maps cannot tell layers
that close apart: within the bias (4 units) the plaza counted as lit and showed white between the
flowers, and farther away, where a cascade's texel is a unit or more wide, the comparison changed
from texel to texel and drew the bands. A smaller bias (0.5 to 1 unit) only softened the bands,
and casting the flowers without the alpha test left them too.

- **Contact zones.** The shadow pass now writes a model caster's depth negative (the R32F maps
  keep the sign; the clear stays 1). Where a tap of the ground's lookup finds a model's surface in
  front of the ground within the bias, or behind it within the slant the cascade's texels reach,
  the ground takes the lightmap's alpha for that tap, the shadow the editor baked, instead of the
  shadow maps' answer. The editor traced rays exactly and baked such contact; the maps keep
  everything farther apart. Models' own receiving is unchanged.
- **The slant grows with the texel.** `GfxShadow.slant` became one value per cascade: the soft
  edge's half width plus the cascade's texel width, times the tangent of the surface's slant to
  the light, the depth one texel spans over a slanted surface. Before, it held the soft edge alone.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, a new scene with the camera zoomed out and
tilted over Prontera's fountain: the beds now show the grey soil between the flowers as they do
without shadows, with the lamp posts' and the fountain's drawn shadows across them, and no
bands. Against the build before, from the same saved camera: 1,411 to 21,458 pixels, along the
beds' outlines, along curbs where the ground meets a model, and on shadow edges; the windmill
sails' shadows on `yuno_gate` are unchanged. The scene harness saves its last camera into
`savedata/OptionInfo.lua` (`Outdoor_ViewDistance`, `Outdoor_ViewLatitude`), so each scene starts
from the one before; comparisons need that file the same before each set.

## No CPU path for the ground and the models (2026-11-09)

Patrick asked why the ground and the models still had a CPU fallback and said it was not needed;
with lightmaps off the ground should only leave the lightmap out, and the frame should save the
work of the shadow maps. Three things sent them to the CPU: a device without the shaders
(`d3dcompiler_47.dll` or shader model 3 missing), which sent the ground, the models, the water and
the granny models there and drew no shadows; lightmaps off (the graphics settings box and
`/lightmap`) or a device without the two-texture blend (`g_waterBumpSupported`), which sent the
ground's surfaces there; and a node or a ground whose mesh could not be made.

- **The client needs the shaders.** `c3d_device_create_renderer` asks `gfx_world_supported`, which
  compiles them on Direct3D 9 (on GL it answers whether there is a context), and without them shows
  a message and makes no renderer, so the client ends as it does when the renderer cannot be made.
  The ground's shader does the two-texture blend itself, so the device's fixed-function support
  for it no longer matters, and `g_waterBumpSupported` and the `waterBump` capability go.
- **Lightmaps off.** The ground's draws bind no lightmap and the renderer leaves stage 1 off while
  it draws the ground's meshes. GL evaluates the stages in its fragment shader and so drew the
  texture times the colour already; the Direct3D 9 ground shader now reads stage 1's colour
  operation from the state cache (pixel constant `c6`) and takes a black, opaque lightmap while it
  is off, which leaves the texture times the colour, what the original drew without lightmaps.
  `renderer_shadow_frame` sets up no shadows then: without lightmaps the original's ground has no
  shadows for the maps to replace. The models' and the ground's in-view casters are now queued
  only while the frame draws shadows (`shadowPending`); before, they were queued every frame and
  dropped unused on maps whose shadow opacity is 0 or with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`. The out-of-view
  walk already stopped at `renderer_shadow_reaches`.
- **Half alpha.** Surfaces with `halfAlpha` were the one part of the ground the meshes left to the
  CPU while the player was not blind. They are now the block's last draws with the colour 1 and
  the alpha 128/255, so a surface whose colour alpha is 0xff gets the original's 0x80, which the
  opaque lists' alpha test (`GREATEREQUAL` 0xcf) drops as it dropped the original's quads. The
  flag's only setter runs while `ray_tests_cells` is set, which nothing in this tree does.
- **Meshes that cannot be made.** A node's mesh takes at most 21,845 faces (three vertices each,
  16-bit indices). The largest node among the 9,614 models in the client's GRFs has 19,085
  (`masin\ice_land.rsm`), so only bad data or a failed allocation leaves a node without a mesh,
  and it is then not drawn; a ground whose blocks cannot be made draws only its water.
- **What goes.** `c3d_ground15_draw_surface` and `off_screen`, the ground blocks' `half` lists,
  the water's screen-space branch, the models' projected triangles (`project`, `face_colours`,
  `on_screen`, `behind_eye`, the two 30,000-vertex buffers and their guard, `MODEL_TL_VERTS`), the
  `clip` argument the screen tests read (`c3d_actor_v*_render`, `c3d_node_v*_render`,
  `c3d_ground15_render`), `renderer_add_two_tex_prim`, the `RENDER_WATER_BASE`,
  `RENDER_WATER_BLEND`, `RENDER_WATER_BUMP` and `RENDER_TWO_TEXTURE_ALT` queues with their flushes
  and the `0x800`/`0x1000` routes, and the helpers only the CPU path used (`uv_turn`, `ground_lit`,
  `SCALED`, `BYTE_R`/`BYTE_G`/`BYTE_B`; the tests keep their own copies as references). The models'
  screen test was the only reader of `g_isVoodooInUse`, the 3dfx Voodoo's guard band; with it go
  that flag, `g_isVoodoo`, the `ISVOODOO` read at startup and `stale_guid`'s answer, which was
  `g_isVoodoo` (it still resets a saved display device that is gone). The granny models keep their
  screen-space branch for a view other than the camera's.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the build of the commit before from
the same saved options: with lightmaps on, the five repository scenes, `yuno_gate`, the far
flower-bed scene, two water scenes and an Izlude scene (20 captures) are identical. With lightmaps
off, against that build's CPU ground with `RAGEXE_SHADOWS=0`: 0 to 335 pixels a capture, rows
where a model lies on the ground (the beds' grass, the feet of walls), the depth ties the ground's
meshes already had with lightmaps on; the models lose the shadows they kept there before.
`test_projection` checks that the shadow frame is not set up without lightmaps.

## The ground's half alpha goes (2026-11-09)

With the ground drawn only from its meshes, the surfaces with `halfAlpha` were the last thing that
kept a split in the ground's blocks (their draws after `plainCount`, outside `castCount`). Patrick
had them removed. The flag was set only by `c3d_ground15_check_alpha`, a ray test from the camera
towards the player that `game_mode_cast_player_ray` ran over the picked blocks' cells while
`GameMode.ray_tests_cells` was set; `game_mode_load_world` sets it to 0 and nothing sets it to
anything else, so no surface ever had the flag and the original's alpha test would have dropped
one that did.

- **What goes.** `GndSurface.halfAlpha`, `c3d_ground15_check_alpha` and `surface_check_alpha`,
  `GameMode.ray_tests_cells` and the loop over the picked cells, and the blocks' `plainCount`.
  A block's draws are now sorted by texture and lightmap only, all with the weather colour, and
  all its indices cast (`indexCount`, which replaces `castCount`). `ray_triangle_hit` stays for the
  attribute map's picking.
- **Tests.** `test_ground_lifecycle` loses the ray test's case and `test_map_entry` the field's
  reset.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the build of the commit before from
the same saved options: the 20 captures of the scene set above are identical with lightmaps on and
with lightmaps off. `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass.

## The camera eases by real time (2026-11-09)

Patrick sent a recording of the client (1920 by 1080 at 30 frames a second, 33 seconds of zooming
in on and tilting over Prontera on a 60 Hz display) that was not entirely smooth. No two recorded
frames repeat while the view moves, so the client presented a frame for every one recorded, but
the zoom between recorded frames jumps within one steady movement (5.5, 12.8, 6.4 per mille of
scale in a row, measured by matching features from frame to frame).

The game advances in ticks of 16 ms (`frame_timer_start(0x3c)`, 1000 / 60 rounded down), and
each frame runs as many ticks as the time since the last one holds (`frame_timer_step_count`),
one call of `view_on_calc_view_info` a tick (one also when there are none). The display waits for
the vertical blank, every 16.7 ms at 60 Hz, so most frames run one tick and every 24th runs two,
more often where a frame's start falls close to a tick's end. `view_process_camera` moves the
camera a tenth of the rest of its way per call, so in those frames the whole view moved twice as
far. The actors' positions follow the server time and their animation frames the time since they
started (`motion_update.c`), so they were even; the camera was what jerked.

- **The change.** `view_process_camera` moves the camera by the real time since its last call
  (`View.easedAt`, the performance counter): the rest of the way times 1 - 0.9^(ms / 16), a tenth
  for 16 ms as one tick moved it, so it keeps the original's speed and converges as the original
  does after a long frame. A frame's further ticks find next to no time passed and move it by
  next to nothing. The division keeps the original's form, `(to - from) / divisor + from`, and
  the divisor for 16 ms is exactly 10, so a run whose frames take 16 ms, as the scene harness's
  do, moves the camera exactly as before.
- **What still steps by ticks.** The effects (`effect_mgr_process`) and the water's animation
  (`c3d_ground15_update_water`) still advance once per tick; they move little of the view.

Validation: the scene set's captures are identical to the commit before (the harness's frames
take 16 ms each). `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass.

## A 24-bit depth buffer (2026-11-09)

Patrick saw things z-fighting when zoomed far out. `pick_zformat` took the original's list
without a stencil, `D16` first, so Direct3D 9 drew with 16 bits of depth (GL already asked for
`GL_DEPTH24_STENCIL8`). A pixel's depth is `(vz - 10) * s / vz` with `s` close to 1, so 16 bits
tell apart depths about vz^2 / 655,360 units apart: 0.24 at the original's furthest zoom (400),
but 1.5 at 1,000, 14 at 3,000, 55 at 6,000 and 153 at the unlocked 10,000 (`Camera: unlock the
zoom and the tilt` drew the view to 40,000 and left the near plane at 10). Captures of Prontera
from 1,500, 3,000 and 6,000 showed the ground covering the flower beds and the fountain, and
walls ragged at their feet.

- **The change.** The list without a stencil now starts with `D3DFMT_D24X8` (then `D24S8`, `D32`,
  `D16`); 24 bits tell apart 0.05 units at 3,000, 0.21 at 6,000 and 0.6 at 10,000. The depth
  biases in normalized depth (the cell markers' 2^-15, the sprites' row and layer steps) keep
  their size.
- **What stays.** At the furthest zoom, layers closer than about half a unit (the beds' grass
  0.3 over the plaza) can still fight; moving the near plane out with the zoom would cure that,
  but the sprites' depth steps are tuned to the present mapping.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the 16-bit build of the commit
before from the same saved options: the far captures differ by 29,149, 64,990 and 99,769 pixels
at 1,500, 3,000 and 6,000 (the beds, the fountain, models' feet); the 20 captures of the scene
set by 267 to 17,368, in rows of pixels where models meet the ground (curbs, planters, the beds'
edges, walls), the depth ties now resolved at 24 bits; sprites, their shadows and effects are
unchanged. `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass.

## Shadows at the furthest zoom (2026-11-09)

Patrick saw no shadows over Prontera from far out at one tilt, and saw them come back when he
tilted the camera up a little. `renderer_shadow_frame` cut the view into cascades between where
its corner rays enter and leave the band around the focus, no deeper than four times the
camera's distance and never deeper than 8,000. Looking down steeply from beyond about 8,000, every
corner ray reaches the band deeper than that, no ray kept any of it, and the frame drew no
shadows; tilting up brought the bottom of the view nearer than 8,000. Captures from a distance of
10,000 at -60 and -70 degrees were the same with and without shadows.

- **The change.** The depth is capped by the view's far plane (`RENDER_FAR_Z`, 40,000) instead,
  so the cascades reach the band at any zoom. Nothing changes below a distance of 1,900, where
  four times the distance stays under 8,000.
- **The light's depth.** The maps keep `SHADOW_DEPTH` (3,000) either way along the light from the
  focus. The largest ground among the client's maps is 2,080 units across (`pay_fild03`), so
  from one corner the other lies at most 2,080 times the sum of the light's two level components
  along it, under 2,950 for any light, as long as the ground is level; it stays.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: from 10,000 at -60 and -70 degrees the town
now has its shadows (18,832 and 20,343 pixels differ from the capture without shadows); the 20
captures of the scene set are identical to the commit before. `build.bat check` and the full
`tests\build.bat` pass.

## Shadows from a flat camera far off (2026-11-11)

Patrick saw no shadows on Prontera's south gate, seen from outside the walls with the camera
tilted almost level. `renderer_shadow_frame` fitted the cascades to the view's four corner rays
alone: the band's depth range was where those rays crossed it, and each cascade covered its
slice's part of each ray inside the band. RO's view is 15 degrees high, so at the flattest tilt
(-5) the upper rays climb 2.5 degrees. From 2,500 units the eye is 218 above the focus, the upper
rays leave the band (300 above the focus) at a depth of 1,866, the lower ones (12.5 degrees down)
reach its floor (60 below) at 1,273, and the focus lies at 2,500: the cascades ended before the
middle of the screen, which had no shadows. A little steeper, the upper rays meet the band only
beyond the depth kept (four times the distance), and a slice that the lower rays crossed only near
its front covered only that part, leaving the middle of the slice off its map. Over tilts from -5
to -85 degrees, half a degree apart, and distances from 100 to 10,000, 50 apart, the focus lay
outside the cascade the shaders pick for it in 1,553 of 32,039 views, all at tilts from -5 to -21
and distances of 1,050 or more: beyond the last cascade at -5 to -9 degrees from distances of
2,300 to 6,100 on, and otherwise off a cascade's map. Captures from 2,500 and 4,000 at -5 degrees
showed shadows only along the bottom edge.

- **The change.** `band_corners` finds the corners of the part of a slice of the view that lies in
  the band: that part is convex, so they are the slice's own corners in the band and the points
  where its twelve edges (the four corner rays and the edges of its near and far rectangles)
  cross the band's two planes. The view's depth range in the band is that of its corners between
  the near plane and the deepest depth kept, and each cascade covers its slice's corners as the
  light sees them; where rounding leaves a slice none, it covers the whole slice, as before. Over
  the same 32,039 views the focus now always lies on the map of the cascade picked for it.
- **What it changes elsewhere.** Where the corner rays already held the band's extremes the depth
  range is the same, and a cascade's square grows only by the points where its slice's rectangles
  cross the band, so its texels may move. In the scene set only the two captures of
  `camera_level_view` (a level camera) change, in the far trees' shading at the top of the screen
  (91 and 47 pixels by more than 16).
- **Test.** `test_projection` looks at the origin from tilts of -5, -8, -15, -35, -55 and -85
  degrees and distances of 150 to 6,000 and checks that the focus lies in the cascade the shaders
  pick for its depth, inside its map. With the old fit it lay beyond the last cascade from -5
  degrees at 2,500 and 6,000 and from -8 at 6,000, and off the map from -8 at 2,500.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`: from 2,500 at -5 degrees the gate, its trees
and the town behind it now have their shadows; from 10,000 at -70 degrees the shadows remain
(21,852 pixels differ from the capture without shadows, 21,731 before); the scene set's other 11
captures are identical. `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass.

## Shadows fitted to the ground and the models (2026-11-11)

The two fixes before this one fitted the cascades better to a guess: that the meshes that receive
shadows lie in a band from 300 units above the camera's focus to 60 below it, out to four times the
camera's distance. It fails wherever ground or models lie outside that band. On 63 of the 926
grounds in the client's GRFs the heights spread over more than the band's 360 units (up to 804, on
`mjolnir_04_1`; `manuk` 736, `ve_fild05` 670, `hu_fild01` 577). A pixel outside every cascade
counts as lit, and on the ground the shadow maps take the place of the lightmap's baked shadows, so
there the baked shadow was taken away as well. Patrick asked for the structural fix; the cascades
are now fitted to where the ground and the models are.

- **The boxes.** `world_build_scene_graph` gives each leaf of the scene graph (32 by 32 over the
  ground) the box around its cells' surfaces, walls included (`groundMin`, `groundMax`): a wall
  rises from its cell's edge to the neighbour's height, which may lie in the next leaf, so the
  cells' tops alone left cliffs' faces out. Each frame `view_shadow_boxes` widens each leaf's box
  by the models in it (`bboxMin`, `bboxMax`, the leaves the scene graph already keeps them in,
  streamed models and skills' models included) and hands the 1,024 boxes to
  `renderer_shadow_frame`. Boxes that are empty or not finite are left out.
- **The fit.** For the view from the near plane to four times the camera's distance, and then for
  each cascade's slice of it, `fit_box` finds the corners of each box's part inside the slice:
  both are convex, so they are the box's corners inside the slice, the slice's inside the box,
  and the ends of each edge's part inside the other. A box wholly inside a slice gives its
  extremes along the view's depth and the light's two axes directly (its centre plus or minus
  half its size along each); a box within the slice's four sides needs only its own edges. The
  cascades' depths run from the nearest to the farthest point found, the last a unit beyond (the
  shaders take the first cascade whose far depth lies beyond a pixel), and each cascade's square
  covers its slice's points as the light sees them. A slice with nothing in it, as between the
  top of a cliff and its foot, takes no casters.
- **Along the light** the maps keep every box, 8 units beyond (`SHADOW_MARGIN`), in place of 3,000
  units either way from the focus; the bias and the slant scale with that range as they did with
  the 6,000 before. The camera's focus is no longer needed and `renderer_shadow_frame` drops it.
- **Cost.** With 1,024 boxes over a 2,000-unit map of random heights, the fit takes 0.11 ms a frame
  from the default camera (488 at -55 degrees), 0.29 ms from 2,500 at -5 degrees and 0.46 ms from
  6,000 at -70 degrees with the whole map in view (`renderer_shadow_frame` in a loop, /O2). Most of
  it is testing every box against five slices; keeping the boxes in view after the first would cut
  that.
- **Tests.** `test_projection` looks from tilts of -5 to -85 degrees and distances of 150 to 6,000
  at flat ground with a hill rising 600 units and a pit 400 deep, both outside the old band, and
  checks that every point on the boxes' faces that the view sees within the shadows' reach lies in
  the cascade the shaders pick for it, inside its map, and that a view that sees none of the boxes
  draws no shadows. `test_scene_ground_box` checks a leaf's ground box: the wall up to the next
  leaf's raised cell, the cells clamped to the ground, an empty leaf and a height that is not
  finite.

Validation, in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1`, against the commit before. On the hilliest
spots of `manuk`, `hu_fild01`, `ve_fild05` and `man_fild03`, from 800 at -40, 1,500 at -20 and
2,500 at -10 degrees, the pixels the shadow maps draw lighter than without them (a baked shadow
taken away) fall in 11 of the 12 captures (from 800 on `hu_fild01` from 29,454 to 14,150: the old
fit drew lit a slope that the editor baked in a ridge's shadow, and the new one shades it), and
rise by 4 in the twelfth. Prontera's south gate from 2,500 at -5 degrees keeps its shadows. The 13
captures of the scene set change by a texel along shadow edges (105 to 316 pixels by more than 16
each, none in `iz_int03_enter`). `build.bat check` and the full `tests\build.bat` pass.

## The renderer's counters without the overlay (2026-11-11)

Phase 0 of `plans/gpu-renderer.md` asks for the renderer's work to be measurable without the
overlay, per scene capture, and for a baseline the later phases are measured against. `g_perf`
(`diag/perf.h`) counted draws, states and texture binds whether the overlay was on or not, but
only the overlay read them, and only the overlay timed anything. Its timer is
`platform_perf_counter`, which the scene harness runs on its frame clock, so within a scene frame
no time passes. The two devices did not count alike either: GL counted render states it changed but
no stage or sampler states and nothing skipped, and counted its blits drawn as quads as draws;
Direct3D 9 counted each sampler state it set, two for a texture address or an anisotropic filter.

- **What is counted** (`diag/perf.h` says exactly): the device's draws after batching (shadow maps
  included) and their primitives, the `gfx_draw` and `gfx_draw_mesh` calls, state changes sent and
  states set to the value they had, texture binds, the bytes of vertices and indices the device is
  given for draws and for a mesh when it fills the mesh's buffers (`vertexBytes`), the texels
  written by `texture_upload_pixels`, `surface_fill_pixels` and the sprite atlas
  (`texture_draw_sprite_frame`, `textureBytes`), and the time spent in `renderer_draw_scene` and
  `view_on_render` (`drawSceneNs`, `viewRenderNs`). The texels and the times are counted above
  `render/gfx.h`; the rest in each device, the same way: one count per `gfx_set_render_state` or
  `gfx_set_stage_state` call (`perf_count_state`), blits as blits only. GL now ignores the texture
  perspective and colour-key states as Direct3D 9 does; it never used them and
  `gfx_get_render_state` already answered `TRUE` for both.
- **The clock.** `platform_stopwatch_ns` (`platform/clock.h`) gives real nanoseconds on every
  platform, and the scene harness's `scene_clock.c` leaves it real while its other clocks follow
  the frames. Each timed call reads it twice; the overlay keeps its own timer.
- **Threads.** The model loader's thread (`world/models.c`) creates and builds textures while
  frames are drawn, so `texCreated`, `locks`, `builds`, `buildsSkipped` and `textureBytes` go up
  atomically (`perf_count_shared`, through the new `platform_atomic_add`), and a texture the loader
  builds counts in the frame during which it does. `resGets` and `resHits` already went up under
  the resource manager's lock. The overlay's own timing of texture locks (`PERF_TEXLOCK`) still
  races with the loader; it is the overlay's alone. Scene runs have no loader thread.
- **The harness.** `drive_state_frame_shown` keeps the counters of the frame being shown and
  starts them again, and `scene.capture` writes `<name>.counters.json` beside each capture: the
  counters of the frame it shows, with the two times in milliseconds
  (`tests/scenes/README.md`). The times are one frame's and are not averaged; they differ by about
  a fifth between runs, so compare several.

Baseline, Direct3D 9 in `client-files` with `RAGEXE_MSAA=1` (the counts are the same in every
run; the times are one run's):

| capture | draws | calls | primitives | states sent / skipped | binds | vertex bytes | texel bytes | scene ms | view ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera_level_view` | 3,345 | 3,631 | 201,876 | 706 / 287 | 2,646 | 43,120 | 0 | 4.37 | 0.72 |
| `camera_level_view_moving` | 3,318 | 3,623 | 201,444 | 706 / 287 | 2,617 | 45,920 | 0 | 4.34 | 0.70 |
| `granny_dead` | 1,140 | 1,179 | 88,945 | 144 / 164 | 1,014 | 301,522 | 0 | 1.19 | 0.54 |
| `granny_dying` | 1,140 | 1,179 | 88,945 | 144 / 164 | 1,014 | 301,522 | 0 | 1.21 | 0.58 |
| `granny_models` | 1,147 | 1,186 | 89,277 | 144 / 164 | 1,021 | 335,066 | 0 | 1.48 | 0.68 |
| `guild_flags` | 1,129 | 1,170 | 86,638 | 144 / 164 | 1,003 | 66,208 | 0 | 1.35 | 0.38 |
| `guild_flags_later` | 1,129 | 1,170 | 86,638 | 144 / 164 | 1,003 | 66,208 | 0 | 1.16 | 0.38 |

Over six runs `camera_level_view` took 4.4 to 5.7 ms in `renderer_draw_scene` and 0.69 to 1.02

## One 64-bit Windows client (2026-11-11)

Phase 0 of `plans/gpu-renderer.md`, decided with Patrick on 2026-11-11: there is no 32-bit client
any more, and SDL is built with its video and GPU API for the phases that use them. Until now
`build.bat` built a 32-bit client by default and a 64-bit one with `x64`. The 32-bit one linked
the three DLLs of the original that exist only for 32-bit Windows (RAD's `mss32.dll` and
`granny2.dll`, and `cps.dll`); the 64-bit one already did without them, as every other platform
does.

- **What went.** The x86 path of `build.bat` (its link line with `lib\cps.lib`, `granny2.lib`,
  `mss32.lib` and `msvcp140.lib`, `/SAFESEH`, `/LARGEADDRESSAWARE`) and the `x64` word and `ARCH`
  switching there, in `tests\scenes\build.bat` and in `vendor\build_vendor.bat`; `lib\cps.lib`,
  `mss32.lib` and `msvcp140.lib`, which only the 32-bit links of `build.bat` and
  `tests\scenes\build.bat` used, and `lib\vcruntime140.lib`, which no link line has named since the
  tree's first commit (`granny2.lib` stays for `tools\granny_export`); `PLATFORM_RAD_DLLS`,
  `GRANNY_IMPORT` and `MSS_IMPORT` with the guards that left `resources/granny_gltf.c` and
  `platform/miles_sdl.c` empty on 32-bit Windows, which now compile everywhere; `__stdcall` on the
  Granny and Miles declarations, on `miles_sdl.c`'s definitions and on the tests' stubs, since no
  DLL is called through them any more, and with it `#define __stdcall` and `#define __cdecl` in
  `platform/win_types.h`, which nothing built off Windows uses now (`platform/thread_win32.c` and
  three Windows-only tests keep MSVC's own `__stdcall` for `_beginthreadex`);
  `_GrannyFreeFileSection` and `_GrannyFreeCompletedModelControls`, which the client never called,
  with their test stubs;
  `tests/scenes/scene_granny_win.c`, which pointed `granny2.dll`'s clock imports at the scene
  clock; and `tests/build_cps_imports.bat`, which checked that the 32-bit exe took `compress` and
  `uncompress` from `cps.dll` (`f9808810`; `docs/upstream/README.md` says why it no longer
  applies).
- **Names.** `build\ragexe.exe` (with `dbg`: `ragexe_dbg.exe`, `freetype`: `ragexe_ft.exe`, `libs`:
  `ragexe_libs.exe`), objects in `build\obj` (`obj_dbg`, `obj_ft`), vendor libraries in
  `build\vendor` (was `build\vendor_x64`, which nothing reads now), the scene harness
  `build\ragexe_scenes.exe` (`ragexe_scenes_ft.exe`). `tests\scenes\build.bat` links every object
  in its folder, so it now deletes them before it compiles: the old 32-bit `scene_granny_win.obj`
  stopped the link.
- **The C runtime.** The client and its variants, the scene harness, every library
  `vendor\build_vendor.bat` builds and the unit tests are compiled with `/MT`, and the client's and
  the harness's links name `libcmt.lib`, `libcpmt.lib`, `libvcruntime.lib` and `libucrt.lib` where
  they named `msvcrt.lib`, `msvcprt.lib`, `vcruntime.lib` and `ucrt.lib`. CMake builds SDL3 and
  FreeType with `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreaded` (FreeType with policy CMP0091 switched
  on, since its CMake files predate it). `vendor\build_vendor.bat` kept its compiler options in
  `CFLAGS`, which CMake also read as the C flags of SDL3 and FreeType; they are `CLOPTS` now.
  `dumpbin /dependents` of `ragexe.exe`, `ragexe_dbg.exe`, `ragexe_ft.exe`, `ragexe_libs.exe`,
  `ragexe_scenes.exe` and `ragexe_scenes_ft.exe` lists no `vcruntime*.dll`, `msvcp*.dll` or
  `api-ms-win-crt-*` set; until now the 64-bit client imported `VCRUNTIME140.dll`,
  `VCRUNTIME140_1.dll` and eleven `api-ms-win-crt-*` sets. `build\ragexe.exe` is 7,110,144 bytes
  (6,719,488 before, with the DLL runtime and SDL's OpenGL). The oracle tests and
  `tools\granny_export` keep the DLL runtime; they link no `build\vendor` library.
- **Old libraries.** `build\vendor` still held the 32-bit libraries in a checkout that had built
  the 32-bit client, and nothing checked what they were: `build.bat freetype`, or the suite run
  before `build.bat`, linked them into 64-bit programs (LNK1112). `vendor\build_vendor.bat` now
  writes `build\vendor\kind.txt` ("x64 /MT, SDL without OpenGL") once all its libraries but
  FreeType are built, and when that file is missing or names anything else it removes
  `build\vendor` and builds everything again, SDL's download included. `tests\build.bat`,
  `build_effect_data.bat`, `build_effect_launch_duration.bat`, `build_effect_trace.bat` and
  `build_jpeg.bat`, which built the libraries only when `yyjson.lib` or `jpeg.lib` was missing,
  call it with the new word `ifneeded`, which returns at once when the file matches.
- **What the player notices.**
  - Players of the 32-bit client, the default until now, hear sound through
    `platform/miles_sdl.c` on SDL3 instead of RAD's Miles. It leaves out speaker types, room types
    and reverb, none of which reached them before: a 32-bit probe of the game's `mss32.dll` found
    "Miles Fast 2D Positional Audio", the provider `contents/sound.c` asks for, answering -1 for its
    speaker type, so the client never applied the `SPEAKERTYPE` setting, and the client only ever
    sets room type 0 and gives every 3D sample an effects (reverb) level of 0. What changes is the
    mixing: `miles_sdl.c`'s distance falloff and left/right balance in place of the provider's,
    SDL's resampling and output device, and `dr_mp3` in place of `mp3dec.asi` for the music. They
    have not been compared with Miles by ear or sample by sample. `mss32.dll`, `mssfast.m3d` and
    `mp3dec.asi` in the game folder are no longer loaded.
  - Granny models (the emperium, the guardians, the guild flag, the treasure box) come only from
    the glTF files `tools\granny_export` writes once per game folder. Without them each model load
    shows "Unable to load file .gr2 (C3dGrannyModelRes :: Load)" and the model is not drawn; the
    first also writes the missing file's name to the debug output, which on Windows is
    `OutputDebugString` and seen only with a debugger attached. With them the models look as the
    table below shows.
  - GRF tables and files and guild emblems inflate, and the emblem cache deflates, through the
    bundled zlib, never through `cps.dll`. A `cps.dll` that does more than zlib (GRF Editor's, for
    the GRFs it encrypts) has no effect: a GRF whose file table needs it does not open
    (`fileio/grf_pak.c:207`), so the client goes without that GRF's files, and a file that needs it
    inflates partly or not at all and reads as truncated data padded with zeros (`grf_pak.c:305`,
    whose result is not checked). Captcha images, which used zlib too, went on 2026-11-02.
  - The client needs no Visual C++ runtime. The game folder's 32-bit `vcruntime140.dll` and
    `msvcp140.dll` served the 32-bit client; a 64-bit program skips them (on this Windows 10 22H2 a
    `/MD` probe copied into a game folder loaded `System32\VCRUNTIME140.dll`), so the 64-bit client
    with the DLL runtime started only where the x64 redistributable was installed.
    `build\ragexe.exe` copied into a copy of `client-files` starts and opens its window.
- **SDL.** `build_vendor.bat` configures SDL 3 at the pinned commit with `-DSDL_VIDEO=ON
  -DSDL_GPU=ON -DSDL_VULKAN=ON -DSDL_OPENGL=OFF -DSDL_OPENGLES=OFF` besides audio (render, camera,
  joystick, haptic, HIDAPI, sensor, power, dialog and tray stay off), which gives the video
  drivers `windows`, `offscreen` and `dummy`, the GPU drivers `d3d12` and `vulkan` and the audio
  drivers `wasapi`, `dsound`, `disk` and `dummy`. The plan uses Vulkan on Windows and no OpenGL, so
  SDL's OpenGL, OpenGL ES and EGL support, on by default, is off: `SDL_windowsopengl.c`,
  `SDL_windowsopengles.c` and `SDL_egl.c` are compiled without their GL code and are not in the
  map. SDL has no option
  for its Direct3D 12 GPU driver: its `CMakeLists.txt` builds `src/gpu/d3d12` whenever
  `check_include_file(dxgi1_6.h)` succeeds, and the same result gives the Windows video driver the
  displays' HDR properties (`SDL_windowsmodes.c`), so the driver stays. `SDL_DIRECTX` stays on for
  DirectSound. `dumpbin /linkermember:1 build\vendor\SDL3-static.lib` lists `SDL_CreateGPUDevice`,
  `SDL_ClaimWindowForGPUDevice`, `SDL_CreateWindow`, `SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface`, `VulkanDriver` and
  `D3D12Driver`. The client calls only audio, but SDL's dynamic API table, on in its static Windows
  build, refers to every function, so the exe links the video and GPU code too (`VulkanDriver` and
  `D3D12Driver` are in the map) and imports `setupapi.dll` and `version.dll` for it, which the
  audio-only 64-bit client of 2026-11-08 did not. `build.bat` already linked both libraries.
- **Who builds 32-bit.** `tools\find_vcvars.bat` gives `vcvars64.bat`, and with `x86` the
  `vcvars32.bat` beside it, for the two scripts whose programs load 32-bit code of the original:
  `tests\oracle` (the original executable; its link now names `/MACHINE:X86`, so a 64-bit
  environment fails at the link instead of building 64-bit tests) and `tools\granny_export`
  (`granny2.dll`; it now compiles zlib in instead of linking `build\vendor\imglibs.lib`). The CMake
  `-A Win32` configuration still builds; its `lua_chunk` is the one that writes
  `tests/fixtures/lua51_win32.lub` with the `.lub` files' 4-byte sizes. `tools\utf8-data`'s
  `luadump` is 64-bit like the client: the vendored Lua reads the `.lub` files' 4-byte sizes on a
  64-bit host, and its dumps of the 23 `.lub` files in `client-files\System` are byte for byte
  those of a 32-bit build. The chunks the tool's tests compile with it now have 8-byte sizes, so
  `Win32ChunkTest` reads that fixture for the 4-byte form: a byte-identical read and write, a
  rewritten constant with a 4-byte length, and `luadump` loading the result. The 45 tests pass.
- **The link check.** `tools/depmap/objsyms.py` gave the link check and the dependency map every
  symbol through `plain()`, which stripped a leading underscore and cut at `@`, for x86's
  decorations. On x64 that renamed real names such as `_AIL_startup` and `_GrannyGetFileInfo`. The
  readers now keep the names of dumpbin and ELF listings and strip the underscore only from a
  Mach-O listing (one whose external symbols all start with it), for the macOS `library_links`
  CTest; `plain()` is gone.

The suite builds 64-bit now; 45 of its steps failed at first. What x64 showed:

- **A bound.** `select_char_init_storage` bounded the character pages by `SIZE_MAX`, which on
  32-bit also kept `per_page * page_count` within an `int`. On x64 a slot count near `INT_MAX`
  passed and the product overflowed. The client never passes one: the counts are three BYTE fields
  of the character list header and the highest slot is a BYTE (`login/char_list.c:103-105`,
  `login/char_info.h`), so there are at most 765 slots; only a direct call, as
  `test_character_preview` makes, reached it. The pages are now bounded by `INT_MAX` as well.
  `main` is 32-bit and does not need it.
- **Narrowing in what the tests compile at `/W3 /WX`.** On x64 MSVC warns where a `size_t` becomes
  an `int` (C4267) and where a window message's `intptr_t` value does (C4244); the client builds
  at `/W1` and never showed them. In the 14 files concerned they are explicit casts now; none of
  the values was a pointer. `text_to_wide` (`core/text_util.c`) leaves a string over `INT_MAX`
  bytes empty instead of handing the conversion a negative length.
- **Stubs.** Thirteen test files defined `mode_send_message`, `ui_window_send`,
  `game_send_message`, `ui_window_mgr_send_msg_`, a window's `send_msg` or `std_sort` with the
  `int` parameters that 32-bit let pass for `intptr_t` and `size_t`; they take the real types now.
  Two of them cut pointers on x64: the effect trace's `game_send_message` read the quake's three
  float pointers through `int`s, and the window lists' generated `ui_window_mgr_send_msg_` (from
  before the message values were widened) recorded the chat text's address as a number. The crash
  dialog's fixture now replaces `GetWindowLongPtrA`, a function of its own on x64.
- **32-bit facts.** Sizes and widths the tests asserted are the x64 ones (`JobHitSounds` 24 bytes,
  `ChatTabs` 16 and `ChatTabSettings` 56, the crash report's 16-digit addresses, the effect
  primitives' 8-byte texture slots), and the frozen path finder's 32-bit layout asserts are gone.
  Cases that only a 32-bit `size_t` rejected (an `INT_MAX` Granny vertex or mesh count,
  `INT_MAX / 3` triangles, a 65,536-square Granny texture, an `INT_MAX`-wide texture upload)
  reach the allocator or the copy on x64 and are gone, or moved to the `int` bounds that still
